sights.n: LUCUA Characters World — Pokémon Center Osaka & Nintendo OSAKA
sights.address: LUCUA SOUTH 10–13F (South Gate Building), JR Osaka Station, Umeda, Kita-ku, Osaka
sights.w: Osaka's answer to Tokyo's Character Street: LUCUA SOUTH opened 5 April 2026 and gathered Pokémon Center Osaka, Nintendo OSAKA and the ONE PIECE Mugiwara Store (moved from Daimaru Umeda) on its top floors, growing to 30+ character shops (Sanrio, Square Enix, Minecraft) by autumn 2026.
sights.anime: Pokémon · Nintendo (Mario, Zelda, Splatoon) · One Piece — Kansai's biggest official character-store cluster, the Pokémon Center and Nintendo flagship stores of western Japan

sights.w: Memorial museum to the 'God of Manga' (Astro Boy, Black Jack, Phoenix) in Takarazuka, the town where he grew up — permanent display of his life and work plus rotating exhibitions, ~30 min by train from Osaka. Note: special long closure 1 Dec 2026 – 4 Mar 2027.
sights.anime: Osamu Tezuka (Astro Boy / Tetsuwan Atom, Black Jack, Princess Knight) — the founding father of modern manga and TV anime, in his hometown

sights.address: Wakamatsu Park, Wakamatsu-chō, Nagata-ku, Kobe, Hyōgo
sights.w: A full-scale 18 m steel Tetsujin-28 robot raised in Wakamatsu Park by the KOBE Tetsujin Project as a symbol of recovery from the 1995 Great Hanshin earthquake; Nagata was creator Mitsuteru Yokoyama's hometown. Short walk from Shin-Nagata Station.
sights.anime: Tetsujin 28-go (Gigantor) by Mitsuteru Yokoyama — a life-size giant robot honouring the Kobe-born manga pioneer and the earthquake recovery

sights.w: Kansai's first Anpanman Children's Museum (2013) at Kobe Harborland: hands-on play museum with daily stage shows and an Anpanman bakery and shop in a free-entry mall — the go-to stop for families with small children.
sights.anime: Soreike! Anpanman (Takashi Yanase) — Japan's best-loved preschool anime hero, with his own bakery-themed museum
